confirmed.title: `enabled:hover:` on .aur-btn removes the hover state from every link-styled secondary button
confirmed.where: src/app/globals.css:292 (`… enabled:hover:border-layer/25 enabled:hover:bg-paper`). Affects about 100 `<Link|a className="aur-btn …">` uses, e.g. home "New opportunity", opportunities "Import from SAM.gov", the proposal page's "View opportunity"/"Back", audit-log "Back to settings", admin/errors "← SuperAdmin portal", and the new not-found.tsx "Solicitations"/"Proposals" links.
confirmed.evidence: In Tailwind 3.4.19 (node_modules/tailwindcss/lib/corePlugins.js:209) `enabled` compiles to `&:enabled`. `:enabled` only matches form controls (button, input, select, textarea, option, fieldset) and never `<a>`. Before the diff, `hover:bg-paper hover:border-layer/25` applied to anchors too. On light theme that hover is bone #F6F7FA → white plus a darker hairline, and it is now gone for every Link button. Only the translateY lift at :316 is left, because `:not(:disabled)` does match anchors. The diff meant to suppress hover on disabled `<button>`s only, but it also stripped the hover feedback from all anchor buttons.
confirmed.fix: Take the `enabled:hover:*` utilities out of the @apply at :292. Put the hover colours in the existing rule at :316, which already uses the anchor-safe selector: `.aur-btn:not(:disabled):hover { border-color: rgb(var(--c-layer) / 0.25); background-color: rgb(var(--c-paper)); transform: translateY(-2px); }` (keep the primary rule separate).

2. **Separation from the muted link went up, not down.** "Forgot password?" is #8F9BB0 in both shots (it is also a link).

3. **Arrow evidence is wrong.** In home--dark after, the arrow's peak pixel is exactly (184,201,255) = #B8C9FF. The quoted #91A0CC is an anti-aliased edge sample. The arrows at src/app/(app)/page.tsx:256-298 are also untouched; the only change in that file is line 72, magenta to violet.

5. **The proposed fix contradicts the design.** Restoring dark cobalt-500 to #4583FF, or hard-picking `text-cobalt-400` for arrows, would undo the documented single dark accent.

Default refuted: this is a design preference, not a regression introduced by the diff. | The colour change is real and the diff did cause it. `teal` is an alias of `cobalt` (tailwind.config.ts:80), so `text-teal` resolves to cobalt-500. The diff moved dark cobalt-500 from 69 131 255 (#4583FF) to 184 201 255 (#B8C9FF) at src/app/globals.css:163. 4. The home Quick-links arrows (src/app/(app)/page.tsx:256,270,284,298) are decorative glyphs inside whole-card `<Link className="aur-card ...">` elements.
